Change 1 removes a box around the Nivia bottle at the far-left edge of crop 3/4. It looks like a real bottle (Nivea facial/micellar product); deleting would lose a real product, though there may be a duplicate with change 3. Change 3 removes a box around the top of the same bottle (the cap area). In crop 4, 3- is at the top of the bottle with the cap, and 1- covers the bottle body. They overlap, so probably duplicates; one of them should be removed, but not both. Change 1 covers the main bottle (the Nivea bottle with white label), while 3 covers the cap region, likely a duplicate fragment. So apply 3, keep 1.

Change 2 removes many boxes in the cotton pad area. These look like thin boxes along shelf edges/price labels, not products (e.g., the shelf edge region around the £1.20 label, the price-tag strip). Removing the ones located at the shelf edge strips and price labels is justified. However, some of them (id 73, 81, 75) are large boxes spanning the cotton roll packages. The cotton rolls in the pink boxes are real products; the large boxes 73, 81, 75 may be a grouping of cotton packs. The two in crop 4, around the purple bottle at the bottom left (id 77 at 0.0389-0.0967, y 0.748-0.758), are thin strips at a price label. Mixed content, but the majority are strips over the shelf edge. Removing the large boxes that cover cotton packs might remove real products. I'm uncertain.

Judging by the other crops, the marks fall on yellow sunglasses, black sunglasses, red frames, and so on. The scene seems to be a collection of sunglasses, and the target is the "sunglasses" category (the reference shows red ones, but the object is likely "sunglasses" in general).

Overall, adding detections of sunglasses is likely justified, since the draft currently seems to contain nothing for these. I'll apply.

The reference is a pair of red sunglasses with dark lenses. The scene has many glasses, and the red sunglasses at the center (around x 0.43, y 0.37) is the main match. The proposed change adds 19 points, none of which are on the red pair. They sit on other glasses (brown sunglasses, yellow, light blue, clear pink frames, and so on). The target object appears to be "sunglasses" in general, but the reference shows a specific red pair with dark lenses, so the task likely intends sunglasses with dark lenses.

The draft presumably already includes the sunglasses, since the change is an add and its points are placed oddly (small marks on lens edges). The added points look like they land on various glasses, including clear-lens eyeglasses (pink at 0.2292, 0.4961 is probably the clear pink pair; 0.7127, 0.8802 is black frames, which are clear-lens; and 0.6731, 0.5599 is pink clear eyeglasses). These are not sunglasses, so some adds are wrong. Duplicates also look likely (0.9253, 0.6641 / 0.9323, 0.6859 / 0.9507, 0.7344 are clustered on the small round sunglasses on the right), and the points aren't centered on objects.

Overall the change is a mixed bag: some points hit real sunglasses, but many are clustered duplicates or on non-sunglasses. I can't reliably accept it as a whole.

The reference is a pale, clear/white-ish marble. Change 1 replaces a mark with essentially the same position (just a re-centering of a marble at the top), which is harmless; keep or apply is basically neutral. Change 2 adds 20 points, many of which land on colored marbles (yellow, orange, blue, red-white) and not on clear/pale ones, so it is unlikely to be fully justified.

Several of the added points appear to sit on clear marbles in the top-left (e.g., at 0.2476, 0.1615 and 0.3405, 0.1146), but many others sit on yellow, orange, or striped marbles (0.5143, 0.1432; 0.6024, 0.1432; 0.9, 0.3411). It's a mixed bag and mostly inaccurate.

Change 1: the replacement is the same location, so no real effect; apply is fine. Change 2: too mixed, so I'll keep the draft.

The reference shows a brown egg carton. In the scene, brown egg cartons are at top center (three stacked, x~0.5, y~0.04, 0.11, 0.18) and the lower middle shelf (x~0.7, y~0.66-0.9, about four cartons).

Changes 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 only shift the x position slightly (replace with minor offsets), so they are plausible and harmless, but whether they improve the answer depends on the box centers. The top cartons span roughly x 0.44-0.56 in the scene, so the center is about 0.5. The shift to 0.5176 is a small change and is fine either way; the boxes at the lower middle span about x 0.57-0.83, so the center is about 0.70. The shift to 0.7031 is also neutral.

Change 3 is identical (no change). The topmost lower carton at y 0.66 is partially visible brown eggs, so keeping it is fine.

Change 7 adds a third carton at the top (y 0.185), which has brown eggs visible at y~0.18 ("7+" mark). In the scene, the carton at y~0.19 with brown eggs appears to be a brown egg carton, so adding is justified.

For the replace changes, the new marks are at the same location within a tiny offset, so they are essentially equivalent. I'll apply them, since the adds are slightly more centered.
